postings.title: Director of Engineering (Data Infrastructure)
postings.text: (P-1490) Databricks processes petabytes of data and billions of transaction events daily - every cluster launch, every query executed, every dollar billed flows through infrastructure that must never fail. When we process billions in billing transactions with 99.999% accuracy requirements, when we ingest terabytes per second across 100+ regions, when a five-minute outage costs millions in revenue and customer trust - infrastructure isn't just important, it's existential. The next phase of our growth demands disaster recovery systems that prove reliability rather than hope for it, testing frameworks that catch production-scale problems before deployment, correctness guarantees that make billing errors structurally impossible, and automation that scales operations sublinearly with growth. In this leadership opportunity, you will build the data infrastructure organization that makes Databricks' continued growth possible. You'll establish foundational teams in Bengaluru owning the bedrock systems that guarantee billing correctness, operational resilience, and zero-downtime recovery across our entire monetization stack, alongside multi-region data ingestion, developer platforms, and deployment automation that eliminate friction at petabyte scale. This isn't about maintaining what exists; it's about architecting the infrastructure that enables Databricks to scale while reducing operational burden. You'll define what world-class infrastructure looks like for the next decade of data platforms. You will pursue these challenges as a founding technical leader in our fastest-growing engineering hub and strategic partner to global infrastructure leaders. In addition to building world-class teams, you will shape architectural decisions that ripple across the company and champion infrastructure-as-product thinking that transforms infrastructure into force multipliers globally. You'll work in an engineering culture born from Apache Spark and open source, where technical depth matters and infrastructure engineers are celebrated as craftspeople. The perfect candidate has built infrastructure organizations at companies where five nines weren't simply aspirational, where petabyte-scale wasn't marketing but Monday, and where the infrastructure team's technical leverage determined whether the business could scale or stall. You have the technical depth to debate data architecture, the strategic vision to define multi-year platform roadmaps, the leadership craft to build teams that top engineers want to join, and most importantly, the conviction that data infrastructure done right doesn't just support the business; it defines what's possible. The impact you’ll have: Deliver the infrastructure vision for systems processing billions in daily billing transactions with zero tolerance for error, building disaster recovery that's provably reliable, testing frameworks that catch what production sees, correctness systems that make billing errors structurally impossible, and observability that predicts failures before they happen Build Bengaluru's data infrastructure organization by establishing it as the destination for India's top infrastructure talent , hiring multiple engineering managers who become force multipliers, and creating a culture where solving hard distributed systems problems at scale is the daily work Own business-critical systems operating 24/7/365 across 100+ regions where even 99.9% uptime means hours of customer pain, driving reliability improvements that prevent millions in revenue loss while eliminating operational toil through frameworks that make systems self-healing, self-tuning, and self-documenting Ship platforms that compound engineering leverage across Databricks: correctness frameworks that catch billing errors before customers do, deployment automation that makes regional expansion push-button, data integration systems that process petabyte-scale flows without human intervention, and testing infrastructure where comprehensive c

postings.location: Central - United States; West Coast - United States
postings.text: GAQ227R127 Databricks is seeking an experienced, highly strategic leader to serve as Director of Order to Revenue Compliance. As Databricks continues to scale, protecting our usage-based revenue engine requires dedicated fiduciary oversight at the intersection of product metering, billing systems, and financial accounting. In this key player/coach leadership role, you will lead a specialized team bridging the gap between raw product metering and financial ground truth. You will oversee usage execution, establish product launch controls, direct partner royalty reconciliations, oversee compliance with partnership arrangements, and serve as the primary compliance lead for usage-related SOX controls and audits. Primary Responsibilities Strategic Team Leadership : Lead, coach, and scale a high-performing team consisting of two functional leads covering Partnerships / Royalty, Money/Engineering Compliance, and Issue Resolution. Actively uphold our culture principles and leadership essentials in daily execution. Usage & Revenue Fiduciary Oversight : Serve as the primary business and compliance oversight body responsible for ensuring all usage-related, financially impacting processes are accurate, complete, SOX-compliant, and validated prior to customer billing and revenue conversion. Partner Agreement & Royalty Governance : Assume complete ownership of outbound/inbound royalty reporting, executions, and complex reconciliations (e.g., Azure/Microsoft, AWS, GCP, SAP). Eliminate manual operational risks, ingestion lag, timing mismatches, and contract-period attribution issues. Cross-Functional System Controls & "Two-in-the-Box" Execution : Partner closely with Engineering (Money Team) and Finance Data Systems (FDS) prior to product launches to validate metering, pricing models, SKU additions, and billing logic against business intent. Audit Ownership & Technical Accounting : Act as the primary audit lead for external audit, internal audit, and executive stakeholders regarding platform consumption calculations and monetization structures. Remediation & Root Cause Analysis (RCA) : Oversee the categorization and resolution of usage issues (Types 1–3), standardize refund SLAs/credits, and drive mandatory cross-functional RCAs with Engineering to prevent systemic metering bugs. Minimum Qualifications Education & Certification : Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related technical field; CPA license preferred. Experience : 12+ years of relevant experience, including extensive experience in revenue accounting, IT audit, and SOX control frameworks. Domain Expertise : Familiarity with ASC 606, specifically applied to consumption-based/usage-based revenue models, SaaS, and complex partner royalty agreements. Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence : Proven track record of managing managers or functional leads while directly collaborating with executive leadership across Engineering, Sales Operations, FP&A, and external auditors. Technical & Analytical Acumen : Ability to bridge technical systems (product metering engines, SQL/data pipelines, sub-ledgers) with accounting rules and complex contract terms. This role is pivotal in delivering exceptional support for our Databricks Data Intelligence platform, addressing complex technical challenges, and ensuring the seamless operation of our data solutions. As a frontline engineer, you will be the primary point of contact for critical issues, working closely with both internal teams and customers to resolve high-impact problems and drive platform improvements. Key Responsibilities: Frontline Support: Serve as the primary technical point of contact for escalated issues related to the Databricks Data Intelligence platform. Provide expert-level troubleshooting, diagnostics, and resolution for complex problems affecting system performance and reliability. Customer Interaction: Engage with customers directly to understand their technical issues and requirements. Provide timely, clear, and actionable solutions to ensure high levels of customer satisfaction. Incident Management: Lead the resolution of high-priority incidents, coordinating with various teams to address and mitigate issues swiftly. Conduct thorough root cause analyses and develop preventive measures to avoid recurrence. Collaboration: Work closely with engineering, product management, and DevOps teams to share insights, identify recurring issues, and drive improvements to the Databricks Data Intelligence platform. Documentation and Knowledge Sharing: Create and maintain detailed documentation on support procedures, known issues, and solutions. Contribute to internal knowledge bases and create training materials to assist other support engineers. Performance Monitoring: Monitor and analyze platform performance metrics to identify potential issues before they impact customers. Implement optimizations and enhancements to improve platform stability and efficiency. Platform Upgrades: Manage and oversee the deployment of Databricks Data Intelligence platform upgrades and patches, ensuring minimal disruption to services and maintaining system integrity. Innovation and Improvement: Stay abreast of industry trends and advancements in Databricks technology. Propose and drive initiatives to enhance platform capabilities and support processes. Customer Feedback: Collect and analyze customer feedback to drive continuous improvement in support processes and platform features. Qualifications: Experience: Minimum of 12 years of hands-on experience in a technical support or engineering role related to Databricks Data Intelligence platform, cloud data platforms, or big data technologies. Technical Skills: A deep understanding of Databricks architecture and Apache Spark™, along with experience in cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, or GCP, is essential. Strong capabilities in designing and managing data pipelines, distributed computing are required. Proficiency in Unix/Linux administration, familiarity with DevOps practices, and skills in log analysis and monitoring tools are also crucial for effective troubleshooting and system optimisation. Problem-Solving: Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues with a strong analytical and methodical approach. Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively convey technical information to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Customer Focus: Proven experience in managing high-impact customer interactions and ensuring a positive customer experience. Collaboration: Ability to work effectively in a team environment, collaborating with engineering, product, and customer-facing teams. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. Advanced degree or relevant certifications are highly desirable. postings.title: Sr. Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) - Communications, Media, Entertainment & Games
postings.text: CSQ127R318 As a Sr. Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) you will work with customers to build and productionize solutions to their data & AI challenges using the Databricks platform. You will own the architecture, lead design decisions, and implement end-to-end systems spanning data engineering, AI, and application development. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering, product, and developer relations. FDEs deliver with customer empathy, integrating with client systems, training, and other technical needs to help customers get most value out of their data. This is a hands-on, customer-facing role for builders who thrive at the intersection of technology and business impact. The ideal candidate combines engineering expertise with adaptability, curiosity, and a passion for working with customers and teammates to solve complex problems that drive measurable outcomes. FDEs are billable and know how to complete projects according to specification with exceptional customer empathy. The impact you will have: Production Solution Delivery: Lead impactful customer technical projects by delivering production-grade systems, designing and building reference architectures, custom applications and data ingestion and ML/AI model integration Transformational Impact: Guide strategic customers as they implement transformational big data projects including end-to-end design, build and deployment of industry-leading big data and AI applications. Work with engagement managers to scope technical delivery work with input from the customer Empower Customers: Guide customers on architecture and design; bootstrap or implement customer projects which leads to a customers' successful understanding, evaluation and adoption of Databricks. Own the Architecture: Lead architecture and design decisions, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable, and aligned with both customer needs and Databricks best practices. Work with the Databricks technical team, Project Manager, Architect and Customer team to ensure the technical components of the engagement are delivered to meet customer's needs. Work with Engineering and Databricks Customer Support to provide product and implementation feedback and to guide rapid resolution for engagement specific product and support issues. Customer Immersion: Embed with customer teams, engaging with stakeholders from technical ICs to executives to deeply understand challenges and deliver impact. Reusable Assets & Scale: Contribute accelerators, frameworks, and best practices that scale impact across accounts and influence the Databricks product roadmap. What we look for: 6+ years experience in data engineering, data platforms & analytics, or software engineering Comfortable writing code in either Python, Scala, JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern frameworks Working knowledge of two or more common Cloud ecosystems (AWS, Azure, GCP) with expertise in at least one Deep experience with distributed computing with Apache Spark™ and knowledge of Spark runtime internals Familiarity with CI/CD for production deployments Working knowledge of MLOps, ML/AI models and AI APIs Design and deployment of performant production end-to-end data architectures and applications that combine data pipelines, ML/AI models, and user-facing interfaces. Experience with technical project delivery - managing scope, timelines and measurable outcomes, translating complex concepts into actionable solutions. Documentation and white-boarding skills. Experience working with enterprise clients and managing conflicts across a broad stakeholder range Build skills in technical areas, and demonstrate curiosity, adaptability, and eagerness to explore new technologies which support the deployment and integration of Databricks-based solutions to complete customer projects. Travel to customers 20% of the time Databricks Certification Pay Range Transparency Databricks is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices

postings.text: As a Sr. Solutions Architect on the team supporting the strategic Digital Natives Business (DNB) customers, you will shape the future of the Data & AI landscape by working with the most sophisticated data engineering and data science teams in the world. postings.text: P-1110 At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We run one of the world's biggest (if not the biggest) data engineering platforms - responsible for processing exabytes of data daily for tens of thousands of customers. We're seeking a dedicated Engineering Leader to spearhead the Pipelines Engine engineering team. The team is responsible for building next generation Runtime ETL features and ensuring that Lakeflow Pipelines has state of art performance for ETL workloads. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites. About the Role Fivetran needs an engineer-architect who can make the AI analyst experience real, dependable, and extensible. This role owns the architecture behind the analyst AI system, including metadata contracts, tool interfaces, context assembly, prompt and skill orchestration, evaluation loops, and the operational patterns that make agents useful in real workflows instead of isolated demos. This is a systems role as much as an AI role. The challenge is not just getting an LLM to do something impressive once. The challenge is building a product-quality analyst system that can reason over schema and business context, use tools correctly, recover from ambiguity, and improve through disciplined evaluation and iteration. This is a full-time, hybrid position based at our Oakland, CA office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including two days in the office each week to connect and build as a team. What You'll Do Define the architecture for the analyst AI stack across prompts, tools, metadata, memory and context strategies, evaluation, and runtime safety. Build the abstractions and interfaces that allow product teams to add new agent capabilities without creating brittle prompt sprawl. Design retrieval and context strategies that give the model the right information at the right time with strong cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs. Establish evaluation loops, benchmark suites, and review processes so model behavior can be measured, debugged, and improved systematically. Partner with product, engineering, and analyst-domain experts to translate real analytical workflows into robust AI-assisted product capabilities. Drive quality standards around correctness, trust, transparency, and failure handling in analyst-facing AI experiences. What We're Looking For Deep experience building AI-enabled product systems, not just running experiments. Strong software architecture skills, especially around APIs, contracts, orchestration, and system boundaries. Practical understanding of LLM prompting, tool use, retrieval, structured outputs, and evaluation methods. Ability to work fluently across backend engineering, product constraints, and user workflow design. Clear judgment about where agent systems should be flexible and where they should be constrain

This role goes well beyond standard engineering. You’ll research emerging techniques in the fast-moving AI landscape and bring real product and market understanding to decide which ideas are worth pursuing — and then you’ll take what you’ve learned and ship it as production software. We’re looking for a true generalist who is willing and able to wear whatever hat the moment calls for: prototyping a new retrieval technique one week, hardening a backend service the next, then doing SRE or QA work when the team needs it. Fivetran AI operates like a startup within Fivetran, and we need engineers who thrive on that range rather than staying in one lane. Fivetran is the epitome of data-driven development — our engineering team is focused on building a world class product that: Builds Infrastructure Agents Can Trust — join our mission to deliver the governed context layer that AI agents depend on: accurate semantic definitions, traceable lineage, data contracts, and auditable history baked in from the start. Embraces Open Standards — help build portable, interoperable data infrastructure: Agents Schema, open formats (Iceberg, Delta Lake), MCP-native interfaces, and connector skills that work with any model and any compute. Scales Without Breaking — work to make Fivetran AI efficient at agent scale, where unit costs deflate as volume grows and context retrieval is fast, accurate, and cost-controlled. We emphasize using no-nonsense tools and take great pride in the simplicity and effectiveness of the systems we build. The Core team is responsible for building, maintaining, and evolving the Rust-based engine that powers dbt Fusion. The team primarily works on the dbt V2 runtime itself, SQL language features powered by Static Analysis, and new ELT primitives. The role sits at the center of several parts of the dbt product: the engine and orchestration, the IDE and developer experience, adapters and data warehouses, and our new compute offering, LakeCompute. You’ll help the team make sound technical and product decisions while keeping a stable GA product moving forward. Partner closely with Product to translate ambiguous requirements into realistic engineering scope, sequencing, and estimates. Help the team balance new feature development, engine maintenance, framework modernization, documentation, and the stability of a GA product. With a greenfield charter, we're building the intelligent layer that transforms Mixpanel from a tool you query into a partner that works for you. We answer the question every data-driven team asks: "What changed, why, and what should I do about it?" We proactively keep users informed about what matters in their data, delivering the right insights and recommendations at the right time, to the right places, both inside and outside of Mixpanel. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it. Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to. We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together. About the Role As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward. This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change. It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone. You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built. If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on. About the Team Klaviyo's Personalization & Analytics pillar builds the intelligence layer that helps marketers understand their customers, personalize every interaction, and prove the impact of their work. Our Personalization SKU — which includes Audience Optimization and our personalization engine — is one of Klaviyo's highest-growth paid products and a cornerstone of our Marketing Analytics & Personalization offering. The Personalization SKU is ML-powered, which means the value it delivers is real and differentiated — but it also means customers need to understand what it's doing before they trust it, and trust it before they pay for it. That gap between "this exists" and "I can't imagine working without this" is where this role lives. About the Role We're looking for a Senior Product Manager who is obsessed with one question above all others: why do customers adopt — or fail to adopt — a product that would genuinely help them? This isn't a traditional growth PM role. We're not looking for someone who runs A/B tests on button colors and calls it a day. We're looking for someone who understands that sustainable SKU growth comes from product quality and value clarity first — and that the best conversion and retention lever is an experience so good that customers can't explain their business performance without it. Your primary mandate is the adoption, retention, and trial conversion of the Personalization SKU. That means owning the in-product experiences that help customers discover Personalization features, understand what they're doing, trust the results, and build habits around them. It means making the ROI of Personalization impossible to miss — not through marketing copy, but through product design. And it means owning the analytics surfaces that make that value visible: the dashboards, metrics, and reporting experiences that connect Personalization usage to business outcomes customers care about. This role sits at the intersection of product intuition, customer empathy, and growth strategy. You'll work closely with the Personalization engineering teams, data science, go-to-market, and customer success to ensure every touchpoint in the Personalization customer journey — from trial activation through long-term retention — is designed with intention and measured with rigor. How You'll Make a Difference Own the end-to-end in-product experience for Personalization SKU trial and adoption — from first contact with an Audience Optimization or personalization feature through the moment a customer builds a sustained usage habit Define and track what real adoption looks like for each Personalization feature — not surface engagement, but the behaviors that actually predict retention and expansion Own the in-product analytics and reporting surfaces that make Personalization ROI visible to customers — the dashboards, performance summaries, and impact metrics that answer "what is this doing for my business?" postings.title: Staff Tooling Engineer
postings.text: Staff Tooling Engineer About the Role The Staff Tooling Engineer is responsible for leading and optimizing tooling development from initial tooling design through mass production sustaining with ODMs (Original Design Manufacturers) and CMs (Contract Manufacturers). This role plays a critical part in ensuring that tooling design meets strict quality, throughput, and cost targets while driving Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) in close collaboration with internal Mechanical Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. The ideal candidate possesses deep hands-on expertise in plastic injection molding, sheet metal stamping, die casting, hydroforming, and tooling fabrication processes, along with proven cross-functional communication and supplier management skills. Your Daily Impact at Peloton DFM & Engineering Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams (ME, ID, Hardware, Quality) to conduct robust DFM/DFA reviews, guiding process selection, material selection, and tooling qualification plans. Tooling Design & Validation: Lead technical reviews for tooling designs, mold layouts, and drawings (including Moldflow simulation, gate placement, cooling, parting lines, and ejector pin layouts). Validate tooling designs with suppliers and toolmakers to proactively troubleshoot issues. NPI Execution: Drive tooling deliverables across all Hardware Product Development phases (Alpha, EVT, DVT, PVT) to support key NPI programs, ensuring timely OK2TOOL and OK2FAB approvals. Supplier & ODM/CM Management: Work closely with ODMs and CMs to manage tooling build progress, trial runs (T1/T2), root cause troubleshooting, and yield improvements on the manufacturing floor. Maintenance & Tooling Audits: Establish and maintain supplier-facing tooling maintenance standards and asset management procedures. Conduct on-site supplier and tooling audits to ensure quality maintenance and mold longevity. PPAP & Quality Alignment: Partner with Quality and Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) teams to establish SOPs for part inspection, technical support for PPAP (Production Part Approval Process), and dimensional/cosmetic qualification. Cost & Capacity Optimization: Assist in building simulation models for tooling and part cost analysis ("should cost"), evaluating factory capacity/capability, and driving continuous improvement initiatives for tooling cost reduction and cycle time optimization. You Bring to Peloton Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Experience: 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience in plastic injection molding, die casting, sheet metal stamping/bending, and tooling fabrication within a high-volume manufacturing environment. Technical Expertise: In-depth knowledge of tool design, tool steel selection, mold/die fabrication, heat treatment, and post-processing (e.g., CNC machining, deburring, plating, surface finishing). Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling (SolidWorks, Creo, or AutoCAD) and simulation software (e.g., Moldflow, CAE tooling analysis). Strong familiarity with DFM/DFA principles, GD&T, engineering drawings, and quality management frameworks (PPAP, ISO/IATF 16949). Problem Solving: Strong analytical and root cause analysis skills (e.g., 8D, DOE, Kaizen, SPC). Communication: Excellent written and oral English communication skills for effective collaboration with cross-functional global teams and international suppliers. Travel: Ability to travel up to 30% to manufacturing facilities and supplier locations as needed. postings.text: Senior Product Designer (Web) ABOUT THE ROLE Peloton is seeking a Senior Product Designer to help define the customer experience on the Web Acquisition team. This role is focused on designing UX/UI for the consumer acquisition experience across the onepeloton.com website. Work closely and collaboratively with UX Researcher, Content Designer, Product Managers, Engineers and various business stakeholders to fulfill the overall product/feature vision. Manage your bandwidth and project pipeline to execute designs in time with your team’s software roadmap. Execute final, “pixel perfect” UI designs and package, spec, and prep for engineering including responsive designs across multi-breakpoints. QA developed features for visual perfection, and provide detailed feedback to engineering towards revisions. Experience designing for various screen sizes for fully responsive web experiences. ● Excellent in interaction design fundamentals, UI design best practices, and accessibility guidelines. Familiarity with agile software development Exists on the cutting edge of UX design – and pushes our user research, testing, and design infrastructure and practices. postings.title: Sr. Product Manager, Menu & 3P
postings.text: Sr. Product Manager, Menu, 3P & Agentic Ordering The Senior Product Manager, Menu, 3P & Agentic Ordering will own the product strategy and roadmap for sweetgreen’s menu architecture and our off-platform channels. That covers third-party delivery marketplaces and new channels such as agentic ordering, where guests order through AI assistants and agents. You’ll own how we build, price, and present our menu on every ordering surface, from our app to Uber Eats to an AI assistant acting for a guest. You’ll also tie the investment in each channel to clear business results. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, finance, and marketing. It needs someone who can turn commercial agreements, technical constraints, and operational realities into a simple guest experience that’s profitable for the business. You will: Set direction and OKRs for menu, 3P, and agentic ordering. Define success criteria where they don’t exist yet, and turn unclear goals into measurable outcomes the team can execute against. Own the 3P channel roadmap , managing the product relationship with delivery partners (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub), including menu syndication, markup configuration, promotions, and platform-specific requirements. Build and scale agentic ordering as a channel. Define how sweetgreen’s menu, customization, pricing, location, and checkout show up when an AI agent orders for a guest. Shape the structured data, APIs, and guardrails that make agent-led orders accurate, on-brand, and conversion-ready. Own end-to-end menu architecture , including item structure, modifiers, pricing logic, and how new products (like Create Your Own and LTOs) are configured across app, web, kiosk, 3P marketplaces, and AI agent surfaces. Tie channel investment to business results. Read performance across channels (order accuracy, menu uptime, partner SLA compliance, conversion, channel profitability, and guest satisfaction) and use those insights to decide where to invest and what to stop. Create and share insights that change how the business thinks about off-platform demand, including how guests discover and order sweetgreen through AI agents compared with marketplaces and owned channels. Lead without authority. Guide a cross-functional team of Engineering, Design, Data, Finance, Marketing, Legal, and Operations toward shared outcomes. Align stakeholders with competing priorities, make clear prioritization calls, and unblock work across teams. Build durable processes and integrated systems for menu publishing and syndication, so a single change flows correctly to every channel. Include Operations needs like Infinite Kitchen constraints, item availability, and 86'ing workflows. Manage tools, vendors, and partner relationships , including some budget responsibility for menu-management platforms, marketplace integrations, and AI platform partnerships. Bring new solutions without being asked. Stay ahead of trends in delivery marketplaces, AI and agentic commerce, and menu personalization, and turn them into bets with clear hypotheses and success measures. Desired traits: A business-minded product leader who reads indicators well, sets OKRs, and ties every roadmap decision to a measurable result A systems thinker who can work through complex integrations across POS, menu-management platforms, marketplace APIs and AI/agent protocols Someone who gives direction in ambiguity, especially in an emerging channel like agentic ordering where the playbook is still being written An influential cross-functional partner who rallies stakeholders and external partners around shared priorities A customer-focused builder who balances margin and operational reality with a smooth guest experience, whether the guest is ordering directly or through an agent A curious, proactive leader who spots opportunities and acts before being asked Desired experience: 5+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years in menu, marketplace/3P, ordering or commerce produc

postings.title: Senior Manager, Loyalty & CRM
postings.text: Senior Manager, Loyalty & CRM sweetgreen is on a mission to build healthier communities by connecting people to real food. We passionately believe that real food should be convenient and accessible to everyone. Every day in each sweetgreen, our 5,000 team members make food from scratch, using fresh ingredients and produce delivered that morning. And in our local communities, we're committed to leaving people better than we found them. We're in the business of feeding people, and we're out to change what that means. Our teams are our most valuable ingredient, the heart of our company, the face of our brand, and what truly makes the sweetgreen experience special and unique. About the Role The Senior Manager, Loyalty & CRM owns how sweetgreen earns attention, frequency, and lifetime value across our owned surfaces. You will lead SG Rewards and the full CRM ecosystem (email, push, SMS, in-app), setting a clear point of view on what makes membership worth having and translating that into audience strategy, personalization, comms and offer architecture, engagement calendar, and a robust test roadmap. This is a strategy-first role. You will define direction across multiple streams (transactional, context-driven, lifecycle, loyalty, promo) before anything gets built, and you connect the loyalty calendar to the broader marketing calendar so every touchpoint compounds to maximize customer and business impact. As a leader, you influence cross-functional teams to bring a shared vision to life that builds true customer loyalty and value for the business, and you develop the team and the CRM & Loyalty function. What You'll Own Loyalty Program Own SG Rewards end to end: member value proposition, earn and burn mechanics, tiers and benefits, activation and engagement layers, and the multi-year roadmap. Build a program that feels distinctly like sweetgreen. Members should be able to describe why it's worth belonging to without mentioning a discount. Sequence loyalty mechanics against the marketing calendar so menu drops, brand moments, and new restaurant openings each land with loyalty-specific value behind them. Evolve offer logic and discount governance in partnership with Finance, optimizing who, what, when, why, and how much to maximize the ROI of every discount dollar and continually strengthen the SG Rewards program economics. CRM and Lifecycle Define what each owned channel is for, how messages sequence across a member's journey, and how frequency is governed across the base. Partner creatively across marketing teams (Brand, Creative, Social, PR, Local) to create engaging campaigns that are distinctively sweetgreen, adapted to each channel and the customer context, and drive conversion and engagement with our customers. Set audience and segmentation strategy grounded in behavior, and refine journeys continuously to eliminate friction in the customer experience. Develop SGs personalization approach across the customer journey in partnership with Product. Lead strategy and concept for lifecycle programs (onboarding, frequency building, deceleration and win-back, tier progression) before execution begins. Own the martech roadmap and vendor strategy, including requirements for future capability needs like decisioning and personalization. Customer analytics and measurement Own the learning agenda: prioritize tests across offer, segmentation, creative, and cadence, and hold the team to a clean read. Report performance in terms of incremental behavior, incremental revenue, and ROI, and translate it into recommendations that shape decisions beyond marketing. Team and operating model Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing team; set clear expectations and grow people into their next role. Steward how the team works cross-functionally: intake, prioritization, briefing standards, QA, and campaign velocity. Evolve the function as the business scales, including where automation and AI decisioning should replace manual work. How We'll Measure Succ

postings.title: Cubist Quantitative Researcher
postings.text: ABOUT CUBIST Cubist Systematic Strategies, an affiliate of Point72, deploys systematic, computer-driven trading strategies across multiple liquid asset classes, including equities, futures and foreign exchange. The core of our effort is rigorous research into a wide range of market anomalies, fueled by our unparalleled access to a wide range of publicly available data sources. JOB DESCRIPTION Researchers are responsible for independently conducting quantitative finance research with a focus on statistical and predictive models. Successful researchers manage all aspects of the research process including methodology selection, data collection and analysis, testing, prototyping, backtesting, and performance monitoring. Some successful researchers have joined us from similar backgrounds at other firms. Others have joined from related fields or directly from academia and have thrived with hands on guidance from our large team of experienced portfolio managers and researchers. Our most exceptional team members combine strong technical skills and a passion for problem solving with an intense curiosity about financial markets and human behavior. DESIRABLE CANDIDATES MS or PhD candidates in finance, computer science, mathematics, physics, or other quantitative discipline 3-7 years of experience in alpha driven quantitative research for equities, futures, fixed income, credit, and/or FX Strong analytical and quantitative skills Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research utilizing large data sets Programming in any of the following: C++, Java, C#, MATLAB, R, Python, or Perl Detail-oriented Willing to take ownership of his/her work, working both independently and within a small team We’re looking for exceptional colleagues with unparalleled passion. If you’d like your resume to stand out, tell us about your exceptional personal achievements, even if they have nothing to do with finance. Of course we love to hear more about specific engineering or data projects that you’ve worked outside of school, or as part of your curriculum. If you’re proud of the work you did we want to hear about it. In addition to exceptional statisticians and engineers, we work with talented musicians, writers, mathematicians, and founders of non-profits; we’d love to learn more about what excites you.

postings.text: About the role Chime's Financial Crimes team protects millions of members from money laundering, fraud, and the organized networks that target consumer financial platforms. We work in a bank-partner model: we run detection and investigation, and we escalate unusual activity to our bank partners, who hold the filing obligation. That means our written work product is read by outside parties, and the quality bar is correspondingly high. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will set the standard for how financial crime work is done here rather than working a queue — defining what good looks like, raising the ceiling for the analysts you lead, and owning the hardest problems on the team end to end. In this role, you can expect to Operate with minimal direction on problems that arrive ambiguous, and you define the approach rather than waiting for one. Move work across team boundaries without formal authority, and you are trusted to represent Financial Crimes to partners outside the function. Raise the ceiling of the people around you — through calibration, coaching, documentation, and the examples you set in your own casework. Improve the system, not just the case. Every hard investigation should leave behind something reusable: a control, a procedure, a detection change, or a documented typology. What you will own: Vendor Management. You will lead, and support, a team of analysts. Vendor team quality. Typology development. You document new and evolving schemes, make them teachable to the wider team, identify if opportunities in coverage are needed, and own the creation of coverage with partners as appropriate. Operational rollout of new coverage. When a new typology or scenario goes live, you design how it will be worked — routing, procedure, evidence standard, and quality checks — before the first alert lands. Procedures and documentation. You own the SOPs for your area and keep them in a state where a third party could read them cold and understand what we do and why. Audit and exam readiness. You prepare the operational side for internal audit, independent testing, and bank partner reviews, and you own remediation of findings assigned to operations through to closure. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less. We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp. This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change. You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better. You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it. This role is for you if you’re excited by: - Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same. - Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality. - Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional. The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path. - Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Monitors submissions of approved time sheets and ensure valid data transfers to/from payroll service. Ensures accuracy of records by maintaining database with updates in status changes, tax withholdings, benefits deductions, time off accruals, etc. Researches and resolves employee inquiries regarding pay, taxes, deductions, direct deposit, garnishments, and leave-related payroll impacts. Provides accurate figures for computing severance and vacation payout amounts as needed. Assists with payroll tax activities including tax notice research, agency correspondence, account reconciliations, and payroll tax reporting support. Develops ad hoc payroll, financial, and operational reporting as required. We are a team of problem solvers and innovators who celebrate our differences and know that our unique perspectives make us stronger and well-positioned for success. We celebrate, and embrace, our team members through our *HUMBLE*HUNGRY*SMART approach, and we believe that we are strongest when we embrace the voices of our employees, customers, partners, and the communities we serve. About the Role: The Director, Quality Control owns Pathward’s first independent Quality Control (QC) function across BSA/AML & Sanctions Operations. Reporting directly to the SVP, Deputy BSA/AML Officer to preserve independence from the production line, the Director sets the strategy, framework, and standards for QC and leads a multi-tier team covering alerts, cases, complex investigations, merchant acquiring, and sanctions. The role designs the QC program, sampling methodology, and error taxonomy; establishes calibration and effective-challenge disciplines; and delivers QC results and thematic trends into BSA/AML governance and to examiners. As a Director-level people leader, the incumbent owns the operating model, budget and resource planning, talent development, and cross-line engagement with Independent Testing, Second Line, and Internal Audit — without assuming production disposition authority. What You Will Do: Own the QC strategy and operating model across all five review populations (alerts, cases, complex investigations, merchant acquiring, and sanctions), ensuring structural independence from production disposition authority. Design and govern the sampling methodology — risk-based and stratified by analyst and queue, with new-hire oversampling and defined statistical confidence levels — and approve periodic recalibration of sample plans. Define and maintain the error taxonomy (critical, significant, administrative) aligned to the OCC five-element documentation baseline, with escalation, root-cause, and re-work rules. Lead and develop the QC team — including a Manager/Lead and QC Analysts — setting goals, managing performance, and building bench strength and succession. Own the calibration program, running monthly calibration between QC, Leads, and Managers with documented outcomes and closure of disputed dispositions. Report QC results and thematic trends into BSA/AML governance and risk committees; provide effective-challenge follow-up and track remediation to completion. Finalize and operate to the Financial Crimes Compliance Independent Testing and Quality Assurance Program Document, and maintain the QC program document set within Doc Control. Coordinate read-only system access (Actimize, FCRM, Bridger) and maintain the QC results repository; ensure QC holds no production disposition rights. Interface with Independent Testing/QA, Second Line, and Internal Audit as a peer — supporting, but never replacing, their functions — and support regulatory examinations and audits with QC artifacts and findings. Own budget, resource, and technology planning for the QC function, including business cases for staffing, tooling, and automation of sampling and reporting What You Will Need: Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred. CAMS required; CFE, CFCS, or CRCM strongly preferred. 10+ years of BSA/AML experience, including quality assurance/quality control or independent testing. 5+ years of people leadership, including leading leaders

postings.title: Senior Product Designer
postings.text: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to join our Product Design team. Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. About the role: Oscar’s Internal Tools design team creates the mission-critical products that power our insurance and care operations. These tools support teams across Clinical, Core Insurance, and Network as they manage complex workflows involving claims, risk adjustment, provider networks, clinical care, and other essential business functions. As a Senior Product Designer, you will help define and deliver clear, effective experiences across this ecosystem. You will work closely with product managers, engineers, researchers, data partners, clinicians, operational teams, and other designers to understand complex problems, identify opportunities, and take solutions from discovery through delivery. The work is operational, workflow-heavy, data-rich, and technically complex. It requires strong systems thinking, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to connect decisions across users, workflows, and products. Your initial product area will be determined based on your experience, interests, and Oscar’s current needs. Oscar is building an AI-enabled design practice. You will use approved tools such as Claude and Codex to clarify problems, explore workflows, identify risks and edge cases, and create realistic prototypes earlier in the design process. You will bring validated directions into Figma for complete state coverage, design-system alignment, and production readiness. You will also help the broader team develop effective and responsible ways of working with AI. This role reports to a Product Design Director. Work Location: This position is based in our Marina Del Rey office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $149,040.00 - $195,615.00 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program, company equity grants and annual performance bonuses. Responsibilities: Independently lead the design process for complex problems, balancing immediate delivery and polish with a coherent long-term direction. Develop a deep understanding of internal users, their goals, and the operational environments in which they work. Partner with Product and Engineering to define product direction, identify opportunities, establish measurable goals, and contribute to roadmaps. Map complex workflows and systems to identify pain points, dependencies, duplication, and opportunities for simplification. Lead design work from early discovery and concept development through detailed interaction design, implementation, and iteration. Use research, data, hypotheses, and experimentation to evaluate ideas and improve product direction. Create prototypes that help teams explore ideas, test assumptions, and build confidence in a proposed solution. Lead workshops, product-vision activities, and presentations when they help teams reach clarity. Use Claude and Codex to clarify user and business needs, explore possible approaches, and identify requirements, risks, and edge cases. Use Claude and Codex to build and test realistic interactions, workflows, and front-end prototypes. Apply strong design judgment to AI-generated output, refining its structure, behavior, accessibility, and visual quality. Partner with engineers to determine which prototypes, patterns, or components can be carried into production. Use Figma to ensure validated concepts have complete states, follow shared patterns, and are ready for implementation.

We don't deliver a clinical program to members. We deploy AI Care Managers, trained on more than 14 million real care interactions, to run the operations of providers, payers and national health systems. It started as an internal problem. On the way to freeing over a million people from pain, Sword hit the same wall every healthcare organization does: we didn't have enough hands to scale the care we needed to provide. Instead of hiring our way out, we built AI to do it, certified it for clinical use, and ran it in our own operations before offering it to anyone else. We've announced a partnership with the Hellenic Ministry of Health to build an AI-powered front door for Greece's 10 million citizens, and we work with other national health systems, health plans and providers across the US and Europe. The US is now our biggest growth opportunity, and this role is central to capturing it. The role We are hiring a Head of Go-to-Market for AI Care Operations in the US. The role sits at the intersection of product marketing, competitive intelligence and commercial enablement. It is one of the leadership roles on the AI Care Operations team, reporting to the General Manager. Here's the opportunity. "AI agents for healthcare" is one of the most crowded categories in the market right now. Voice AI startups, EHR vendors, care management platforms and outsourcers all claim to automate care operations, and to a buyer they can sound alike. postings.text: Position Summary The Physician Advisor (1099 Contractor) is a licensed physician responsible for conducting clinical discussions with treating providers regarding utilization management determinations. The physician applies Medicare/CMS requirements, applicable medical necessity criteria, health plan policies, and clinical judgment to determine the appropriate level of care and/or medical necessity of requested services. The role supports timely, consistent, evidence-based utilization management while providing treating physicians an opportunity to discuss relevant clinical information before or following an adverse determination, as applicable. Key Responsibilities Conduct scheduled and ad hoc peer-to-peer discussions with treating physicians and other qualified providers regarding inpatient, outpatient, post-acute, and other authorization requests. Review the member's clinical documentation, utilization management review, applicable criteria, and rationale for the proposed or issued determination before the P2P discussion. Evaluate medical necessity and the appropriate level of care, including inpatient versus observation/outpatient status when applicable. Apply CMS Medicare Advantage requirements, the Two-Midnight benchmark, applicable NCDs/LCDs, MCG or other approved clinical criteria, and health plan policies as appropriate. Discuss the clinical rationale for determinations clearly, professionally, and collegially with treating providers. Consider additional clinical information presented during the P2P and determine whether it changes the medical necessity determination. Approve or overturn a proposed adverse determination when newly presented information supports coverage, within delegated authority and organizational policy. Escalate complex, high-risk, or unclear cases to the appropriate Medical Director or clinical leadership. Document P2P discussions accurately and contemporaneously, including the clinical information discussed, physician participants, outcome, and rationale. Complete P2P requests within established regulatory and organizational turnaround times. Identify recurring clinical, documentation, criteria, or provider-education opportunities and communicate trends to UM leadership. Collaborate with nurses, medical directors, appeals and grievances, provider engagement, and other operational teams as needed. Maintain confidentiality and comply with HIPAA, CMS, accreditation, and organizational requirements. Lead case review discussions on clinical JOCs Qualifications MD or DO from an accredited medical school. Current, unrestricted U.S. medical license. Board certification in an appropriate clinical specialty; Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Emergency Medicine, or another specialty with broad medical experience preferred. Minimum of 5 years of clinical practice experience preferred. Experience with utilization management, medical necessity review, physician advisory services, payer medical review, or hospital case management strongly preferred. Experience with Medicare Advantage and CMS medical necessity/coverage requirements preferred. Familiarity with MCG, InterQual, CMS coverage policies, and the Two-Midnight rule preferred. Strong physician-to-physician communication skills and the ability to manage difficult or disputed clinical discussions professionally. This is your chance to make a real impact on the lives of millions by driving advancements in healthcare security — ensuring utmost compliance and privacy while enabling engineers to move fast and safely. Candidates must be within commuting distance to New York City WHO YOU ARE - A Security-First Thinker: You instinctively design systems that are secure by default, and you know how to balance security rigor with engineering velocity. - An AI-Savvy Engineer: You're energized (not intimidated) by the rapid adoption of AI-assisted development and see it as an opportunity to build novel security frameworks. - A Trust Builder: You communicate effectively across engineering, compliance, and leadership teams — authoring clear, plain-spoken technical proposals that drive alignment. - A Learn-it-all: You stay ahead of emerging threats and continuously evolve your approach — from adversarial ML to supply chain attacks on AI pipelines. - A Leader at All Levels: You're hands-on in code and architecture, but you also mentor others and help the team self-organize around measurable outcomes. This is a high-ownership, systems-first role within the team. You'll set technical direction for a platform that's mid-consolidation. Carving a clean domain boundary out of an existing service, closing known correctness gaps, and negotiating the contracts that other teams build against. You'll work closely with product and data science, and have a direct line to business outcomes like referral conversion and cost-per-acquisition. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own the technical direction for the Incentive Platform. Carve a dedicated domain out of its current home, with enforced boundaries and a facade other services call instead of reaching into internals. - Generalize eligibility and entitlement logic into real, owned APIs, replacing duplicated caps and ad hoc scripts with a single source of truth for what a member has earned and is owed. - Run production data migrations. Dual-write, backfill, cutover on a system with financial and compliance stakes, where correctness during the transition matters as much as the end state. - Negotiate and build the technical contract with Fulfillment: idempotent order creation, failure handling, real-time inventory, and reserve/release semantics. You're the technical counterparty other teams negotiate with, not just an implementer of their asks. - Find and close correctness gaps in the current system. Places where real dollar-value entitlements are miscounted, under-specified, or rely on an undocumented assumption. - Partner with product, design, and analytics to define what to build and why, balancing short-term wins with long-term platform leverage. - Raise the engineering bar by driving code quality, system design standards, observability, and technical decision-making on the team. - Mentor engineers on the team, growing their judgment on architecture and cross-team tradeoffs over time. - Participate in the team’s weekly on-call rotation, helping ensure the reliability and timely support of the systems we build. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR - Domain modeling under legacy constraints - You've carved a bounded context out of a service with accreted responsibilities, without a rewrite, while it kept shipping. - Production migration experience - You've run a dual-write/backfill/cutover on a real data model, ideally with financial or compliance stakes where getting it wrong is expensive. - Full-stack depth - Strong skills across technologies such as React, React Native, TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Node.js, relational and non-relational databases, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, and Redis. We don’t expect a perfect match on every technology, but you should be fluent in most. - Staff-level leadership - You’ve set technical direction for a team, influenced cross-functional roadmaps, and made architectural decisions that have held up over time. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS - Bachelor’s degree (or foreign equivalent) in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field. - 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, including meaningful time working on production systems at scale. - Hands-on experience building and operating full-stack applications (for example, using React/React Native on the frontend and Node.js/TypeScript or similar on the backend). PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Experience designing or evolving incentive, rewards, ledger, or entitlement systems that carry real financial or compliance stakes. - Experience running a production data migration (dual-write, backfill, cutover) without a maintenance window, on a system where correctness during the transition mattered. - Experience negotiating or owning a service contract with another engineering team — API design as a cross-team negotiation, n

postings.title: Medical Director, Care & Case Management
postings.text: Role overview The Medical Director, Care Management leads the care, case, and utilization management programs, setting clinical direction and owning program performance for Included Health's CCM and UM programs. This physician leader is first a strong operator. The person owns outcomes, not just clinical standards, with success defined as the program hitting its performance and quality targets. This role owns a critical program that bends the cost curve: navigating members to high-quality care, educating members about their health, and supporting them during vulnerable moments. Reporting to the Senior Medical Director, Complex Care, they bring a strong, evidence-based point of view, are comfortable operating under ambiguity, and translate organizational priorities into clinical operations that perform at scale. They are responsible for ensuring the programs contribute to clinical outcomes, client commitments, and third-party oversight. This physician leader leads an innovative, fast-moving team at the core of Included Health’s population health strategy. Key Responsibilities:: Clinical and Operational Leadership: Serve as the clinical escalation point for care, case, and utilization management programs. Set and maintain clinical standards, evidence-based care pathways, and clinical quality expectations across the portfolio, using clinical judgment in collaboration with subject matter experts. Own clinical KPIs, including setting targets, evaluating performance gaps, and redesigning workflows to close them. Interrogate the data. Identify outliers or workflows that don't make sense, and drive them to resolution and improvement. Run the program's operating cadence, including weekly performance reviews, escalation triage, and action tracking, to the team accountable to committed targets and timelines. Program Design and Strategy: Evolve the clinical operating model across adult, maternity, and pediatric populations to deliver on Included Health’s population health strategy. Partner with Product and Engineering to design, validate, and deploy AI and agentic tools into clinical workflows, and ensure AI-generated output is valid and actionable. Build new programs and models of care, and define how they scale across populations and clients. People Management: Lead, manage, and develop leaders, setting clear clinical and operational expectations. Conduct performance reviews, coaching, and feedback for direct reports. Attract and retain a strong, diverse pool of clinicians and talent aligned with company vision and goals. Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner with other clinical leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to coordinate care for members with multi-specialty needs. Represent care management in cross-functional initiatives, pilots, and strategic planning related to complex care. In partnership with the Quality team, implement quality assurance processes to ensure consistent, excellent service to members. Qualifications:: Required: Education: Medical Doctor (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO). Clinical Experience: Board certified in internal medicine, family medicine, med-peds, or a related specialty, with a minimum of 7 years of post-residency clinical experience, and the ability to apply that clinical lens to population health leadership. Leadership Experience: Minimum of 5 years in a healthcare leadership role with direct oversight of clinical teams or programs, including experience managing other clinical leaders (managing managers). Licensure: Active, unrestricted medical license in good standing in state of residence, plus active multi-state licensure or willingness to obtain it. Operations and Performance: Track record of delivering against operational KPIs, like productivity, clinical quality, engagement, in a scaled, performance-driven setting. Work until 9-6PM (local hours) Be comfortable discussing several medical conditions and experience with populations across the age ranges Spanish speaking desirable Experience working remotely, and strong competence and ability to use multiple computer/medical record systems. Strictly follow security and HIPAA regulations to protect our patients' medical information. Be pleasant, responsive, and willing to work with and learn from our team. A lot of time is spent on the phone with patients and families, and a lot of time communicating with colleagues. postings.title: Virtual Primary Care Nurse Practitioner
postings.text: At Included Health, we’re redefining what it means to have access to great healthcare. We’re seeking board-certified Family Nurse Practitioners to join our Virtual Primary Care team. In this role, you’ll provide comprehensive, ongoing care to patients of all ages nationwide through video and phone visits; helping them understand not just what their care plan is, but how and why it supports their health. The ideal candidate is skilled at managing their own patient panel, fostering lasting relationships, and working closely with a multidisciplinary team to deliver compassionate, patient-centered care. They communicate clearly in patient-friendly language, and demonstrate the ability to balance multiple priorities in a high-volume clinical environment. Above all, they are passionate about raising the standard of healthcare for everyone. Responsibilities: : Provide high-quality virtual primary care through video visits, including assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and patient education. Manage a panel of patients, delivering comprehensive care across acute, chronic, and preventive needs. Collaborate with the Care and Case Management team to develop care plans and support successful outcomes. Partner with supervising physicians as required by state and practice guidelines. Work with the Credentialing Team to obtain additional state licenses as needed. Maintain patient satisfaction and quality metrics by practicing evidence-based medicine with exemplary bedside manner. Utilize telehealth technology to deliver patient care, while effectively managing multiple tasks in a fast-paced clinical environment. Stay current with medical knowledge, treatments, and medications. Adhere to assigned schedules, including some evenings and weekends. Strictly adhere to HIPAA and security regulations to safeguard patient information Contribute to a culture of humility, curiosity, and collaboration. Required Qualifications: : Minimum of three years experience delivering primary care in an ambulatory/outpatient family medicine or internal medicine setting. Experience independently managing a patient panel as the designated primary care provider. Active, unrestricted Nurse Practitioner and RN license in state of residence; ability to be licensed in additional states as required. Multi-state licensure highly preferred Current and active board certification by a national certifying body through ANCC or AANP. Must maintain active Medicare status and not be excluded, sanctioned, or reprimanded by any state or federal healthcare program (including Medicare/Medicaid), the OIG, or the GSA. Comfortability addressing a broad variety of medical conditions, including acute and chronic conditions as well as preventative issues. Ability and willingness to treat all ages across the lifespan. Must have a professional, private, and secure home office environment for virtual patient visits. Demonstrated ability to provide empathetic, compassionate care and support to patients and families during challenging situations. Ability to manage high patient volumes and competing priorities in a dynamic clinical environment while maintaining quality of care. Strong proficiency with technology and electronic health platforms; experience with telehealth preferred. Weekend hours may be split between Saturday and Sunday, with a rotational day off around the worked weekend. All schedule templates and changes require approval and are subject to operational needs. postings.text: As our Director, Staffing Transformation & Operations, you will lead a critical transformation in how Member Care scales across staffing strategy, workforce management, vendor strategy, and AI enablement. postings.title: Engineering Manager - Member Experience
postings.text: Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease. Job Overview: We are hiring an Engineering Manager to run a squad that builds Omada's Member-facing systems. A squad owns problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what it ships. You own that squad: what it works on, in what order, and how the people in it grow. As an Engineering Manager, you ship code alongside your Builders. You own the execution and will run the squad’s rituals: iteration shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation - these are your calls. Owning the call means having a point of view on the tradeoffs behind it, and partnering with your stakeholders to work through the problems that surface along the way. You partner closely with a Product Strategist who spends their time in front of members, coaches, and stakeholders, and who prototypes to test ideas quickly. They own what the squad should build and why. You own whether the squad can deliver it, at what cost, and by when. You set the quality bar and the operational standard for your squad and will be empowered by both tooling and adaptable processes to hold it. About you: You are comfortable being accountable for what your squad ships. You still write code, and you want to. This role ships production work every sprint, off the critical path, in the same codebase and the same agent workflows as your squad, so you feel the friction your people feel first-hand. You are a product engineering leader: you are opinionated about the product you own. You understand the why behind its existence, and you own the what and the how. You are respected technically, but you do not need to be the strongest engineer in the squad. Your work stays off the critical path for exactly that reason, so the squad never waits on a merge request you did not get to because a people conversation ran long. You are opinionated about where AI-assisted development helps and where it creates rework, and that view comes from doing the work rather than reading about it. Above all, you are enthusiastic about providing the best possible care for our members, and about building the best engineering team of your career. What you'll be doing: Own the squad's delivery. Sprint shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation. Make the calls, write them down, and be accountable for them. Own cycle time . This is yours to improve, not at the expense of quality, and yours to explain when it changes. Ship code. Production work every sprint, off the critical path, using the same agent workflows your squad uses. This is what earns you the standing to review their work and the credibility to defend the model. Partner with your Product Strategist. They own what the squad builds; you hold the line between their scope and yours so the squad never has two people answering the same question differently. Grow your engineers. Omadans care about each other: we believe everyone can grow, and you will provide your reports with the best leadership they have ever experienced. Own the operational health of your squad. On-call rotations, MTTR and post-incident analysis are shared work you lead. Escalate early, often, and precisely. You bring tradeoffs, you use your engineering and product taste backed by data to come up with recommendations. Hire the new generation of AI-augmented Omadans. We believe in co-intelligence: we will continue hiring amazing humans, and show them why they need to build a career with us. What you need for this role: 6+ years in software engineering, including at least 2 years managing engineers, or equivalent experience leading delivery for a team you were accountable for. A track record shipping mission-critical software to production, and living with it afterwards. We all make mistakes; what sets you apart is that you own yours and turn them into something better. Experience owning prioritization and estimation for a team, including saying no, not now, and
